steps.text: Four Years Ago...
3:25 P.M. \ Overcast
Saint-Marsol's College, Auchterigg District of Londinium

steps.name: Naughty Child
steps.text: Hey! Look, all the soldiers in Parliament Square, all the crossbows and cannons! You've got nowhere to run!

steps.name: Innocent Child
steps.text: *whimper*...

steps.name: Naughty Child
steps.text: Stop crying, you're not supposed to cry! Chin up! You're playing the King!

steps.name: Innocent Child
steps.text: Um... I-I'll have you all killed! I-I've got my Kn... Knights of the Foyer!

steps.name: Naughty Child
steps.text: It's the Knights of the Tower.

steps.name: Naughty Child
steps.text: Most of them surrendered. And all the ones who won't give in will be like you soon. They'll be tried by us, and... the fiery rage of Londinium we represent.

steps.name: Innocent Child
steps.text: W-Who can try a king?

steps.name: Naughty Child
steps.text: Used to be nobody could, maybe nobody else in the future either.

steps.name: Naughty Child
steps.text: You're a dead-end, Your Majesty. You blocked Victoria's forward stride.

steps.name: Naughty Child
steps.text: Every machine in the city stopped on your command, plus you wanted to take the daily bread away from all the suffering people, stealing every last penny out of their purses.

steps.name: Naughty Child
steps.text: Our hands toil for nothing but tomorrow's sun. It's you and your greedy attendants that forced us... to stain ourselves in your blood!

steps.name: Naughty Child
steps.text: Forward, soldiers! For Victoria!

steps.name: Innocent Child
steps.text: Victoria...! I... I am Victoria... you insolents! Victoria won't pardon you for this, even if I become a s... s...

spans.text: am Victoria... you insolents! Victoria won't pardon you for this, even if I become a s... s...

steps.name: Naughty Child
steps.text: A specter! Speeec-teeer! First you run over to those steps, and then fall down, and then you say that!

spans.text: A specter! Speeec-teeer! First you run over to those steps, and then fall down, and

steps.text: Who's that running around the doorway here?
Ralph, Anna, you little pair of mischief-makers—

steps.name: Innocent Child
steps.text: It's Miss Molly...

steps.name: Naughty Child
steps.text: We were just getting to the most fun part! Anna, quick, get on the steps, we're going to do the hanging!

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: Hanging... hanging?!

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: Who taught you children such a cruel game?

steps.name: Naughty Child
steps.text: It's how the grown-ups in Slantwards Alley play.

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: Slantwards Alley... there's all manners there. Did you watch some kind of silly show? Who took you to see?

steps.name: Naughty Child
steps.text: Tom the cobbler.

steps.name: Naughty Child
steps.text: He was drinking a lot of yellow stuff, and it was all dripping off his face. And then he ran up on stage while they were up there, and he was yelling and screaming 'I won't let you disgrace His Majesty the King, he was a great among greats.'

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: That bloody Tom! No, that's no language to use in front of children... Oh, what's he thinking, taking children to a pub?!

steps.name: Naughty Child
steps.text: Let's keep going, Anna. I want to play one more time before supper.

steps.name: Innocent Child
steps.text: Then it's your turn to be the one that dies! Ralph, you promised! You can't fib!

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: Oh, Your Majesty... pardon these children for disrespecting you.

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: They've never seen you, nor heard your voice before. All they know are rumors of you from all the city's gossip peddlers.

steps.name: Naughty Child
steps.text: Miss Molly, you've never seen the King before either! You don't get to be all hoity-toity with us!

steps.name: Naughty Child
steps.text: Come on, run, Anna, I'm chasing you—

steps.name: Innocent Child
steps.text: Out of the way, t... traitor! Sooner or later, you'll all be torn apart by the beasts within!

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: Children, this is hardly proper of you.

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: If you don't want punishment, you'd best cut that out. Never let any of the clergy or teachers see...

spans.text: If you don't want punishment, you'd best cut that out.
let any of the clergy or teachers see...

steps.text: See what?

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: Oh, good, Lady Golding!

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: Ralph, why are you so flushed?

steps.name: Naughty Child
steps.text: Um, 'cuz... 'cuz...

steps.name: Innocent Child
steps.text: We're playing a game, ma'am. It's really fun.

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: A game?

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: Very well, I understand. Return to your bedrooms soon, and don't forget to do today's homework.

steps.name: Innocent Child
steps.text: Yes, ma'am.

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: Additionally, Ralph, Molly may only be older than the two of you by a few years, but she is still your teacher.

steps.name: Naughty Child
steps.text: Yes, ma'am. Sorry, Miss Molly—

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: Alright, alright, listen to the ma'am now. Off you go.

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: I can't believe you didn't scold the two of them.

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: Ralph and Anna? I don't blame them.

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: The children just don't understand what cruelty is yet.

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: They have an innate desire to learn. If they can't learn anything proper from books or ourselves, it's only natural they'll turn to other places.

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: They... so many say that hanging transformed Victoria. Lady Golding, do you agree?

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: Ask the same question to different people, and you'll only get different answers.

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: The machines of Highbury's munitions factories certainly never ceased to whir, but the grand houses of Auchterigg have had many a change in ownership.

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: While all I know is that these poor children still come in droves to our school each year, bless their hearts. They're in need of help, much as I was twenty years ago.

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: I thank the school. If it hadn't lodged me, I would have long died of some illness or other.

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: Molly, what happened just earlier gave me an idea.

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: An idea... You're mean, the sets of plays you're holding?

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: Indeed.

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: So they're meant for the children. But they've only just learned to read. Won't it be a little too soon?

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: Better this than all the showy, slipshod stuff in Slantwards Alley.

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: For young children, acting others' roles is tantamount to a game. The complex implications might escape them for now, but at least they can get a little taste of the emotion and power within the words for themselves.

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: I do hope you're right.

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: It comes with another upside too, no? The children won't be nodding off in my literature classes anymore.

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: Haha, I suppose so. What matters to me is that we can use up just a little of their energy—it'll be a great relief for me!

steps.name: Londinium Citizen
steps.text: Excuse me, madams, bookshop's closing in advance.

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: Mr. Adams? You're quite early to shut today.

steps.name: Londinium Citizen
steps.text: Haven't you heard yet, ma'am? There was a disturbance at the Duke's office in Camden this morning.

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: Disturbance? What kind of disturbance is it to affect Auchterigg? It's quite a ways away.

steps.name: Londinium Citizen
steps.text: One of the office admins got beat to death. Duke of Stafford's nephew, apparently. Only just rocked up in Londinium a week ago.

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: ...Oh, rest his soul. Have the police caught the murderer yet?

steps.name: Londinium Citizen
steps.text: That's the problem.

steps.name: Londinium Citizen
steps.text: Witnesses say the suspect scarpered into a Defense Force barracks.

steps.name: Victorian Soldier
steps.text: Seal the street! Move! Don't let him get away!

steps.name: Victorian Soldier
steps.text: All eyes out—

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: And now he's fled into Auchterigg? Really?

steps.name: Londinium Citizen
steps.text: Hard to say, ma'am. Probably not that simple.

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: How strange. Are these the Defense Force's men? My eyes might just be playing tricks, but their uniform seems a little different to what I remember...

spans.text: these the Defense Force's men? My eyes might just be playing tricks, but their uniform seems a little different to what I remember...

steps.name: Londinium Citizen
steps.text: I've got a friend who lives in Camden, ma'am. He says there's soldiers just flooding the street nearby, all of them wearing that uniform.

steps.name: Londinium Citizen
steps.text: There's even word that... well...

steps.name: Londinium Citizen
steps.text: A duke secretly slipped into Londinium just yesterday!

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: How, though? Wasn't that prohibited by law?

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: Thank you, Mr. Adams. These books are too heavy; I'll pick them up next time.

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: Molly. Back to the school, as quick as we can.

steps.name: Victorian Soldier
steps.text: No one? Didn't they say they saw someone hiding in the alley?

steps.name: Victorian Soldier
steps.text: We can't let word of the Duke spread in the city! If we do, our entire operation today's... ugh, damn and blast!

steps.name: Victorian Soldier
steps.text: Didn't even see if it was a man or a woman. What the hell are these intelligence agents doing in their bloody Londinium offices?

steps.name: Victorian Soldier
steps.text: Good-for-nothings! Got the Duchy's people running circles around them!

steps.name: Victorian Soldier
steps.text: Lucky I just landed a bolt—

steps.name: Victorian Soldier
steps.text: Keep up the chase! They can't have gotten far!

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: Wait—

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: Lady Golding? Did you see something?

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: Nothing urgent.

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: Molly, you go back to the school for now. Gather all the children, and make sure they don't stray out into the streets.

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: What about you?

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: I'm going to see a friend. Prepare some hot water and a clean towel in the office for me; I'll be back as soon as I can.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: Rrmph... *pant*...

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: Sorry, bear with me. School things are fairly rudimentary—more often we have children falling over while making a racket. Not so much being shot by soldiers' crossbows.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: Who knew... you could sew up wounds.

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: With the scant yearly donations to the school, we can't afford to hire that many staff. I have to moonlight as the school nurse a lot of the time.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: Urrrgh... ow...

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: After seeing you move so silently on the street, I wasn't imagining you would feel the pain.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: Oh, don't jest with me... you're the only one in all of Londinium who I can truly catch my breath with.

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: I can suture your wound, Heidi, but I can't disinfect it. You'd best be off to a hospital straight away.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: I don't think so.

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: Can you tell me why?

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: I thought we were friends.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: Golding, I shouldn't have come here with you in the first place. I haven't wanted to pull you or the children into all the mess.

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: So the soldiers are after you. Are they really the Duke of Stafford's men?

spans.text: after you. Are they really the Duke of Stafford's men?

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: Did Adams tell you that...? I thought he would keep mum.

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: He's your friend, and mine as well. He was the one holding the book club we met each other at, and don't you forget that.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: Ha, ha. Could I ever?

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: You were a ruthless one then.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: 'A fast-food work of pop-culture subservience.'—'Its only use is fueling chatter between ladies of the house and girls at teatime.' Your words for my newest work.

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: But I did say that the author's talent lay far beyond.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: And I hadn't conceived that the most tasteful of all Londinium's critics was such a simple, unassuming teacher.

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: I could read into every line you'd written, and for each one, the hundred lines you hadn't besides—those were your words, Heidi, uttered by you.

spans.text: I could read into every line you'd written, and for each one, the hundred lines you hadn't besides—those were

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: Never would I doubt the unspoken understanding between us.

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: Then let me help you.

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: We can be more frank with each other, Heidi... just as we always have.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: Golding... did I ever tell you that, years and years ago, I had the fortune of meeting a Laterano cleric who wasn't a Sankta?

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: She once lived in Londinium too. She may well have some ties to this school's origin.

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: Who is she?

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: She's...

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: Lady Golding, goodness!

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: Oh, hold on, you have a guest? Wh—Who might this be...?

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: A literary circle friend.

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: Is something the matter, Molly?

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: Outside, ma'am... I thought you would've heard...
From far away come strange noises.
The sort that Londiniers are quite inured to.
They confuse them all too easily, at first, with the sound of an exploding steam boiler carelessly lit, or the sound of the mechanical fowlbeasts the children so love slicing through the air.
But as the ground and building tremors become steadily apparent, an instinctual panic strikes everyone.

By protection of the kings, Londinium has never once met Catastrophe before. What they face now is without a doubt a different sort of menace—and in those of long age, something stirs. The nightmare of twenty years ago has come again.
The sign of war.
In the midst of the room's silence, the rumble grows thicker.

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: It doesn't make sense.

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: They were only catching a few criminals. Why'd they bring out such a display of force?

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: If we could make sense of every thought in the minds of our fellow man, many a tragedy would never come to pass.

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: Molly, if you could check whether the soldiers in the street are still there.

steps.name: Molly
steps.text: Yes, ma'am.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: I have to leave now.

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: I know. I'd love to urge you to stay, but I know full well that not even heavy artillery could stop you.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: I know you've noticed too, Golding. Another scene change is being wrought upon Londinium tonight.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: The Duke of Stafford's troops are on the offensive at Parliament Square as we speak. The Duke of Cavendish's men arrived at the outer wall a long time earlier.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: The coup d'état over twenty years ago, and the turmoil it brought, were at least the briefest thing for the citizens here. But this time... I couldn't say.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: This will likely develop into an inter-ducal war, and its epicenter will have been Londinium.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: I've... come into some intel. It has the potential to save tens of thousands of lives. The sort of thing I need to deliver out of the city before tomorrow's daybreak.

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: ...War, you say.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: I'm afraid so.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: The fire of war could spread to other cities at a moment's notice. Every Victorian needs to make preparations.

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: Victoria's peace has endured for over two decades since His Majesty's passing. Many call it a miracle, but I long ceased to believe it a miracle of any sort.

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: No one would abandon their own interest, especially when its vastness is that of Victoria's... It instead gave those with the stuff to plunder it all the more to consider.

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: We pitiful that live in this crack of history could only simply shut our eyes and proclaim it so. 'Peace.'

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: Heh... who would've thought deathly illness would drive Stafford to such measures? And who could've predicted how the other dukes would respond?

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: Without the efforts of people such as yourself, this war would've broken out twenty-two years ago, instead of being delayed to today.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: Are you trying to soothe me, Golding?

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: I'm only stating the reality, nothing more.

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: You needn't reveal your goals to me, Heidi, let alone explain what your people have been planning all these years.

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: You need only answer me one thing—will peace come again?

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: ...It will.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: That's what we've been striving for all along.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: We will protect our homeland. That is the truth, throughout the ages, that we Victorians have believed in.

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: Even if countless will die in the streets outside? Even if, with each end in sight upon the road of yours, the next preordained war comes to greet you?

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: Indeed.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: Because war will ultimately end. It may end at the hands of us, or our posterity. When the smoke clears from the skies shrouding Victoria, no more will the children's smiles be crossed with haze.

spans.text: ultimately end. It may end at the hands of us, or our posterity. When the smoke clears from the skies shrouding Victoria, no more will the children's smiles be crossed with haze.

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: Very well.

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: I'm willing to believe in you, Heidi, to try and believe.

steps.name: Heidi
steps.text: Should I ever be able to return to Londinium, Golding... then I'll tell you everything, when we meet again.

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: Remember that. Remember your promise.

steps.name: Golding
steps.text: ...Come back alive.
